questions.q: What does `readFile(path, "utf-8")` return, compared to calling `readFile(path)` with no encoding argument?
options: It returns a plain string instead of a raw Buffer of bytes
It returns a Promise that never resolves
It deletes the file after reading
It returns the file size in bytes only
questions.explain: Without an encoding, readFile resolves with a Buffer (raw bytes); passing "utf-8" decodes it into a plain string, which is what you want for JSON or text files.

questions.q: Why is the synchronous fs API (e.g. readFileSync) considered dangerous to use inside a server like the one built in Lesson 36?
options: It blocks Node's entire single-threaded event loop until the read finishes, stalling every other request the server is handling
It cannot read JSON files, only plain text
It is not supported on Windows
It automatically deletes the file after reading
questions.explain: Sync fs calls block the whole event loop; in a single-threaded server handling many requests concurrently, one blocking file read stalls all of them, unlike the non-blocking fs/promises API.

questions.q: What problem does `path.join(process.cwd(), "data", "cache.json")` solve compared to manually concatenating strings with "/"?
options: It automatically creates the "data" folder if missing
It encrypts the resulting path
It makes the file read faster
It uses the correct path separator for whatever OS the script runs on (backslash on Windows, forward slash on macOS/Linux)
questions.explain: Manually concatenating with "/" breaks on Windows, which uses "\" as its path separator; path.join picks the right one automatically for the current platform.

questions.q: In the lesson's caching example, why is `existsSync("cache.json")` checked before calling `readFile`?
options: To avoid readFile throwing an error on the very first run, when the cache file doesn't exist yet
Because readFile cannot accept a path that might not exist, under any circumstances
Because existsSync deletes old cache files automatically
existsSync is required syntax for every fs/promises call
questions.explain: readFile throws if the file doesn't exist; checking existsSync first (a fast, synchronous existence check) lets the function return null gracefully on the first run instead of crashing.

questions.q: Why does caching the last-checked block number to a local JSON file matter for a script that queries an RPC endpoint?
options: It has no real benefit, it's purely stylistic
It avoids wasting rate-limited RPC calls on re-querying data that hasn't changed
It permanently stores a copy of the entire blockchain
It replaces the need for an RPC provider entirely
questions.explain: Public and even paid RPC endpoints rate-limit requests; a small local cache avoids redundant calls for data that rarely changes between runs.
